visualContent.text: The human heart is organized into four chambers: right/left atria for receiving blood and right/left ventricles for pumping. A thicker left ventricular myocardium handles the high-resistance workload of systemic ejection.

textContent.heading: Chamber Architecture and Valvular Mechanics
textContent.body: Atrioventricular valves (tricuspid and mitral) use chordae tendineae anchored to papillary muscles to prevent leaflet prolapse during ventricular systole. Semilunar valves (pulmonary and aortic) guard ventricular outflow tracts without chordae. Unidirectional valve opening and closure coordinate diastolic filling and systolic ejection.

conclusion.statement: Integrated anatomy, electrical timing, and valve mechanics drive effective dual-circuit perfusion.
supportingPoints: Dual circuits balance low and high pressure flow.

essentialPoints: Cardiovascular system consists of a muscular pump (heart) and a closed vascular network
Dual-circuit architecture couples pulmonary reoxygenation with systemic tissue perfusion
Organization into four discrete chambers: right/left atria and right/left ventricles
Thicker left ventricular myocardium reflects high resistance workload of systemic ejection
Tricuspid and mitral AV valves tethered by chordae tendineae to papillary muscles to prevent systolic prolapse
Pulmonary and aortic semilunar valves guard ventricular outflow tracts without chordae tendineae
Unidirectional valve opening and closure coordinate ventricular filling (diastole) and ejection (systole)
Ejection from right ventricle into pulmonary trunk and pulmonary arteries toward alveolar beds
Capillary gas exchange releases carbon dioxide and absorbs oxygen
Oxygenated venous return via four pulmonary veins into the left atrium
High-pressure ejection from left ventricle into the aorta to supply peripheral body tissues
Microvascular solute, nutrient, and metabolic waste exchange across capillary networks
Systemic venous capacitance return via venae cavae into the right atrium
SA node initiates spontaneous action potentials as the primary intrinsic cardiac pacemaker
AV node delays electrical impulse to allow complete atrial emptying before ventricular contraction
Bundle of His, bundle branches, and Purkinje fibres rapidly activate ventricles from apex upward
Bulk delivery of respiratory gases, substrates, and metabolic waste products across capillary networks
Cooperative maintenance of physiological acid-base balance alongside renal and respiratory organ systems
Baseline adult parameters: typical resting heart rate of 60–100 beats/min and cardiac output of ~5 L/min
Interdependence between mechanical valve integrity, sequential conduction, and hemodynamic balance
Dual circuit arrangement ensures distinct low-pressure pulmonary gas exchange and high-pressure systemic delivery
